title: INDIA bloc MPs march to ECI headquarters against 'vote theft' and electoral roll revision
seoTitle: Delhi march against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

tea.why: Protesters allege irregularities in electoral roll revision, question the Election Commission's neutrality, and claim "vote theft" by the BJP.
tea.want: Protesters demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and seek to save democracy.
tea.changed: Oct 6: Police briefly detained several opposition lawmakers, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, during their march.

summary: Opposition parties, including the INDIA bloc and the Cockroach Janta Party, launched a series of protests on October 2 in Delhi against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. On October 6, INDIA bloc MPs marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission of India headquarters, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police deployed hundreds of security personnel, barricaded routes, and briefly detained several lawmakers, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, who were attempting to reach the ECI office. The Election Commission and the BJP have denied the accusations, while the Supreme Court agreed to hear legal arguments regarding the poll body's voter drive.
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
End alleged irregularities in electoral roll revision
response: Police deployed hundreds of security personnel, including paramilitary forces, and erected barricades to prevent protesters from reaching the ECI office. Several lawmakers were briefly detained. The BJP dismissed the protest as an attempt to "relaunch Rahul Gandhi" and denied the allegations. The Election Commission of India also…

crowd.text: Around 140 MPs have hit the streets in Delhi to protest

arrests.text: Several opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, were briefly detained

updates.text: Opposition parties and civil society groups began protests against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
Three women journalists alleged sexual harassment by police personnel during a previous demonstration at Jantar Mantar.
India's Supreme Court agreed to hear legal arguments seeking its intervention in accusations against the poll body's voter drive.
INDIA bloc MPs, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission office.
Police deployed body cameras on personnel managing the protest, following recent sexual harassment allegations.
Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and several other opposition lawmakers were briefly detained by police.
Rahul Gandhi stated that around 300 Opposition MPs wanted to meet the Chief Election Commissioner but were stopped by police.
